what: Two photo rows move in opposite directions (top row left, bottom row right) at .3px per frame. On scroll they instantly speed up by the distance moved per frame ×.3 (max 4px), then settle back to normal speed over 1.5s with power3.out. They pause when off-screen.

options.speed: px flowing per frame at normal speed (60fps), default .3 — scaled by time between frames so speed is the same regardless of screen refresh rate
options.max: Max speed attached by scroll (px/Frame), default 4
options.gain: Follow speed per 1px of scroll, default .3
options.settle: Settling length (seconds), default 1.5 — at 0, no tween: every frame it adds the scrolled amount (signed) × gain directly within ±max. Scrolling up slows, then flows in reverse, and Lenis deceleration is the settling (Studio)
options.[data-fx-part=row]: Line (child) — the 2nd and 4th lines flow the opposite way
options.[data-fx-part=track]: Band inside a row — the same cells are chained in twice
options.cycle: Seconds to flow one set’s width — if given, this replaces speed for measuring the normal pace (Brand 120)

use:
Five cells + the same five cells
…

from.where: index.html .hm-mid__track (one strip of photo windows — original function.js setMidSlider: half width ÷ 120s flow + clamp(lenis.velocity × 60 × .3, ±200px/s), no tween → one frame with gain .3 · max 3.33)
